q-125422.problem: If ${\int }_{C}z\,\text{d}x+x\,\text{d}y+y\,\text{d}z$ is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ for some piecewise smooth curve $C,$ then $F(x,y,z)=$
q-125422.worked_solution:
Given a piecewise-smooth path $C$ and a vector field 

$$
F(x,y,z)=P(x,y,z)\,i+Q(x,y,z)\,j+R(x,y,z)\,k
$$

defined on $C,$ we have

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{C}P\,\text{d}x+Q\,\text{d}y+R\,\text{d}z
$$

In our case, $P=z,Q=x,R=y.$ Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}(z\,i+x\,j+y\,k)\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{C}z\,\text{d}x+x\,\text{d}y+y\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $F=z\,i+x\,j+y\,k.$

q-125411.name: Question 2
q-125411.problem: Let $F(x,y,z)=yz\,i+xz\,j+xy\,k$ and let $C$ be a path in ${R}^{3}.$ Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r?$
q-125411.worked_solution:
Given a piecewise-smooth path $C$ and a vector field 

$$
F(x,y,z)=P(x,y,z)\,i+Q(x,y,z)\,j+R(x,y,z)\,k
$$

defined on $C,$ we have

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{C}P(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x+Q(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y+R(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z.
$$

Therefore, in our case, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{C}yz\,\text{d}x+xz\,\text{d}y+xy\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

q-125411.html:
Question 2
?

Let F(x,y,z)=yzi+xzj+xyk and let C be a path in R3. Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr?

a
∫Cxdx+ydy+zdz
b
∫C(yz+xz)dxdy+xydz
c
∫C(yz+xy+xy)dxdydz
d
∫Cyzdx+xzdy+xydz
e
∫Cyzdx+(xz+xy)dydz
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Given a piecewise-smooth path C and a vector field F(x,y,z)=P(x,y,z)i+Q(x,y,z)j+R(x,y,z)k defined on C, we have

∫CF⋅dr=∫CP(x,y,z)dx+Q(x,y,z)dy+R(x,y,z)dz.

Therefore, in our case, we obtain

∫CF⋅dr=∫Cyzdx+xzdy+xydz.

q-125419.name: Question 3
q-125419.problem: Let $F(x,y)={e}^{y}\,i+{e}^{x}\,j$ and let $C$ be the path defined by $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2},\,t-1⟩$ for $t\in [0,1].$ Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r?$
q-125419.worked_solution:
Given a piecewise-smooth path $C$ and a vector field 

$$
F(x,y)=P(x,y)\,i+Q(x,y)\,j
$$

defined on $C,$ we have

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{C}P(x,y)\,\text{d}x+Q(x,y)\,\text{d}y.
$$

Therefore, in our case, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{C}{e}^{y}\,\text{d}x+{e}^{x}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Let F(x,y)=eyi+exj and let C be the path defined by r(t)=⟨t2,t−1⟩ for t∈[0,1]. Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr?

a
∫Ceydx+exdy
b
∫Cey2dx+ex−1dy
c
∫Cex−1dx+ey2dy
d
∫Cex+ydxdy
e
∫Cex2dx+ey−1dy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Given a piecewise-smooth path C and a vector field F(x,y)=P(x,y)i+Q(x,y)j

defined on C, we have ∫CF⋅dr=∫CP(x,y)dx+Q(x,y)dy.

Therefore, in our case, we obtain

∫CF⋅dr=∫Ceydx+exdy.

q-125417.name: Question 4
q-125417.problem: Let $F(x,y)=4\,i-(2y-3x)\,j$ and let $C$ be the path defined by $r(t)=⟨t,\,3t-1⟩$ for $t\in [0,1].$ Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r?$
q-125417.worked_solution:
Given a piecewise-smooth path $C$ and a vector field 

$$
F(x,y)=P(x,y)\,i+Q(x,y)\,j
$$

defined on $C,$ we have

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{C}P(x,y)\,\text{d}x+Q(x,y)\,\text{d}y.
$$

Therefore, in our case, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{C}4\,\text{d}x-(2y-3x)\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

q-125416.problem: Let $F(x,y)=(x-3y)\,i+2\,j$ and let $C$ be the path defined by $r(t)=⟨t,\,{t}^{2}+1⟩$ for $t\in [0,1].$ Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r?$

$$
F(x,y)=P(x,y)\,i+Q(x,y)\,j

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{C}P(x,y)\,\text{d}x+Q(x,y)\,\text{d}y.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{C}(x-3y)\,\text{d}x+2\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}

q-125416.html:
Question 5
?

Let F(x,y)=(x−3y)i+2j and let C be the path defined by r(t)=⟨t,t2+1⟩ for t∈[0,1]. Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr?

a
∫C2dx+(x−3y)dy
b
∫C(x2+1)dx+ydy
c
∫C(y2+1)dx+xdy
d
∫Cxdx+(y2+1)dy
e
∫C(x−3y)dx+2dy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Given a piecewise-smooth path C and a vector field F(x,y)=P(x,y)i+Q(x,y)j

defined on C, we have ∫CF⋅dr=∫CP(x,y)dx+Q(x,y)dy.

Therefore, in our case, we obtain

∫CF⋅dr=∫C(x−3y)dx+2dy.

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $C$ is the closed polygonal path $OABO,$ shown in the diagram above, traversed in the counterclockwise direction?
q-76473.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can represent $C,$ which is traversed in counterclockwise, as the union of $3$ paths:

$$
C={C}_{1}\cup \{-{C}_{2}\}\cup {C}_{3},
$$

where $-{C}_{2}$ is the same path as ${C}_{2}$ but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{-{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r-{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ∫CF⋅dr, where C is the closed polygonal path OABO, shown in the diagram above, traversed in the counterclockwise direction?

a
−∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
b
−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
c
∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
d
∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
e
∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that we can represent C, which is traversed in counterclockwise, as the union of 3 paths:

C=C1∪{−C2}∪C3,

where −C2 is the same path as C2 but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $C$ is the closed polygonal path $LMNL,$ shown in the diagram above, traversed in the counterclockwise direction?
q-77146.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can represent $C,$ which is traversed in counterclockwise, as the union of $3$ paths:

$$
C={C}_{1}\cup \{-{C}_{2}\}\cup {C}_{3},
$$

where $-{C}_{2}$ is the same path as ${C}_{2}$ but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{-{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r-{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ∫CF⋅dr, where C is the closed polygonal path LMNL, shown in the diagram above, traversed in the counterclockwise direction?

a
∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
b
−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
c
∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
d
−∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
e
∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, notice that we can represent C, which is traversed in counterclockwise, as the union of 3 paths:

C=C1∪{−C2}∪C3,

where −C2 is the same path as C2 but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

∫CF⋅dr=∫C1F⋅dr+∫−C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr=∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr.

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $C$ is the closed polygonal path $PQRP,$ shown in the diagram above, traversed in the counterclockwise direction?
q-77134.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can represent $C,$ which is traversed in counterclockwise, as the union of $3$ paths:

$$
C=\{-{C}_{1}\}\cup {C}_{2}\cup {C}_{3},
$$

where $-{C}_{1}$ is the same path as ${C}_{1}$ but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{-{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & =-{\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r.\end{aligned}
$$

q-77134.html:
Question 8
?

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ∫CF⋅dr, where C is the closed polygonal path PQRP, shown in the diagram above, traversed in the counterclockwise direction?

a
−∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
b
∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
c
−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
d
∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
e
−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that we can represent C, which is traversed in counterclockwise, as the union of 3 paths:

C={−C1}∪C2∪C3,

where −C1 is the same path as C1 but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

∫CF⋅dr=∫−C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr=−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14223647/assets/9fd222d255fd1a37f00cbe7c9abf6af0d0e3af92f9ac581591bb1062780e69fa.png)

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $C$ is the closed polygonal path $ABCA,$ shown in the diagram above, traversed in the **clockwise** direction?
q-76476.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can represent $C,$ which is traversed clockwise, as the union of $3$ paths:

$$
C=\{-{C}_{1}\}\cup {C}_{2}\cup \{-{C}_{3}\},
$$

where $-{C}_{1}$ and $-{C}_{3}$ are the same paths as ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{3}$ but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{-{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{-{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & =-{\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r-{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ∫CF⋅dr, where C is the closed polygonal path ABCA, shown in the diagram above, traversed in the clockwise direction?

a
−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
b
∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
c
∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
d
−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
e
∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, notice that we can represent C, which is traversed clockwise, as the union of 3 paths:

C={−C1}∪C2∪{−C3},

where −C1 and −C3 are the same paths as C1 and C3 but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

∫CF⋅dr=∫−C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫−C3F⋅dr=−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr.

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $C$ is the closed polygonal path $TUVT,$ shown in the diagram above, traversed in the **clockwise** direction?
q-77138.worked_solution:
First, notice that we can represent $C,$ which is traversed in clockwise, as the union of $3$ paths:

$$
C=\{-{C}_{1}\}\cup {C}_{2}\cup {C}_{3},
$$

where $-{C}_{1}$ is the same path as ${C}_{1}$ but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{-{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & =-{\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{3}}F\cdot \text{d}r.\end{aligned}
$$

q-77138.html:
Question 10
?

Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ∫CF⋅dr, where C is the closed polygonal path TUVT, shown in the diagram above, traversed in the clockwise direction?

a
∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
b
∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
c
−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
d
−∫C1F⋅dr−∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr
e
−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr−∫C3F⋅dr
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that we can represent C, which is traversed in clockwise, as the union of 3 paths:

C={−C1}∪C2∪C3,

where −C1 is the same path as C1 but traversed in the opposite direction.

Therefore, we obtain

∫CF⋅dr=∫−C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr=−∫C1F⋅dr+∫C2F⋅dr+∫C3F⋅dr.

The path ${C}_{1}$ consists of a line segment from the point $A(-2,2)$ to the point $B(-1,2),$ and the path ${C}_{2}$ consists of a line segment from the point $B(-1,2)$ to the point $D(-1,0).$

Given that ${\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r=-\frac{7}{2},$ evaluate ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=(x-y)\,i+(y-x)\,j,$ and $C={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}.$
q-77185.worked_solution:
We will use the fact that

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r.
$$

We're given the value of the first integral, so we only need to work out the second.

The path ${C}_{2}$ is the vertical line segment from $B$ to $D.$ It can be parametrized as

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{2}(t) & =b+t(d-b) \\  & =⟨-1,2⟩+t(⟨-1,0⟩-⟨-1,2⟩) \\  & =⟨-1,2-2t⟩ \\  & =-\,i+(2-2t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0<t<1.$ Along this segment, we have $x=-1$ and $y=2-2t.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{2}(t)) & =(x-y)\,i+(y-x)\,j \\  & =(-1-(2-2t))\,i+(2-2t-(-1))\,j \\  & =(-3+2t)\,i+(3-2t)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivative, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{2}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-1)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2-2t)j \\  & =-2\,j\end{aligned}
$$

We can now compute the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{2}(t))\cdot {r}_{2}^{′}(t) & =((-3+2t)\,i+(3-2t)\,j)\cdot (-2\,j) \\  & =(3-2t)\cdot (-2) \\  & =4t-6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r \\  & =-\frac{7}{2}+{\int }_{0}^{1}F({r}_{2}(t))\cdot {r}_{2}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\frac{7}{2}+{\int }_{0}^{1}(4t-6)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\frac{7}{2}+[2{t}^{2}-6t]_{0}^{1} \\  & =-\frac{7}{2}+[2({1}^{2})-6(1)-0] \\  & =-\frac{7}{2}-4 \\  & =-\frac{15}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{1}(t)) & =(x-2y)\,i+(y-x)\,j \\  & =((-2+2t)-2t)\,i+(t-(-2+2t))\,j \\  & =-2\,i+(2-t)\,j.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{1}(t)) & =x\,i+y\,j \\  & =t\,i+{t}^{2}\,j.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{1}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})j \\  & =i+2t\,j\end{aligned}

We will use the fact that

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{{C}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}r+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}r.
$$

We're given the value of the first integral, so we only need to work out the second.

The path ${C}_{2}$ is the line segment from $A$ to $B.$ It can be parametrized as

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{2}(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =⟨2,0⟩+t(⟨1,1⟩-⟨2,0⟩) \\  & =⟨2-t,t⟩ \\  & =(2-t)\,i+t\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0<t<1.$ Along this segment, we have $x=2-t$ and $y=t.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{2}(t)) & =(x+y)\,i+(x-y)\,j \\  & =(2-t+t)\,i+(2-t-t)\,j \\  & =2\,i+(2-2t)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivative, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{2}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2-t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)j \\  & =-i+j\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}F({r}_{2}(t))\cdot {r}_{2}^{′}(t) & =(2\,i+(2-2t)\,j)\cdot (-i+j) \\  & =-2+(2-2t) \\  & =-2t\end{aligned}

$$
